parts.text: Which claim correctly distinguishes the two processes?

options.text: Breathing is the physical movement of air in and out; respiration is the chemical release of energy inside the body.
Respiration produces oxygen, which breathing then carries out of the body.
Air moving into the lungs is a chemical process because it happens inside the body.
Respiration is only a physical process because no new substance can be seen forming.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Ira breathes in and out while resting. Inside her body, sugar is broken down with oxygen and energy is released.

part_answers.answer: Breathing moves air; respiration chemically breaks down food with oxygen to release energy.

teacher.key_rationale: Breathing is physical air movement; respiration is chemical energy release with oxygen and food. Reversing which process makes oxygen, calling lung air movement chemical, or treating respiration as only physical all miss that hinge.
